planned_outcome: Land HMS Triumph: 1D Stefan moving-boundary inverse problem with latent-heat phase change. Forward solver via enthalpy method; joint 4-parameter inverse (x_core alpha_dough alpha_crust rhoL_eff) + comparison against literature-pinned 1-parameter fit. actual_outcome: 1D Stefan-front inverse problem with enthalpy-method forward solver delivered. Forward solver matches Stefan-Neumann analytical within 2.82 deg C (PASS). Synthetic recovery clean: 10/10 converged, bias 0.05 (smearing-mismatch artefact), RMSE 1.0-1.5 deg C. Real-CSV joint 4-param fits well-conditioned: max |rho| 0.30 (vs M7's 0.91 — degeneracy GONE). 6 of 7 BA3C cases extrapolated past T1 (x_core in -0.05 to -0.06). BUT real-CSV RMSE = 6-10 deg C, identical to M7 heat-equation baseline. Driver auto-verdict NO-GO; admiral assessment is more nuanced — see admiral note in commit.
success_metric_result: Forward solver passes analytical sanity. Synthetic recovery RMSE 1.4 deg C (vs M7's 6 deg C). Real-CSV joint RMSE median 6.91 deg C (M7 6.48 deg C). Inverse well-conditioned at max |rho| 0.30 (vs M7 0.91). 4/7 BA3C cases extrapolated past T1.

adopt: Enthalpy method (effective Cp with smearing window) for moving-boundary problems — non-stiff, uses standard ODE solvers, well-suited to inverse problems
Generate synthetic test data via DIFFERENT numerical realisation than the inverse-fitter (different smearing dT) to avoid self-test tautology
avoid: Treating headline RMSE alone as the verdict — Stefan vs heat-eq RMSE were similar but well-conditioning, x_core extrapolation, and physical interpretability all differ
